title: Burst knots: latency-cost vignette (tiling vs multiplex interplay)
content:
Purpose
- Short sketch: explore a small set of tiling vs multiplex runtime configs to understand p50/p90/p99 behavior and cost under short, intense bursts (knots) versus steady background traffic. This is a lightweight collateral draft intended for the console UX and ops playbook.

Experimental setup (fast sketch)
- Hardware: 1x A100-80GB (baseline) and 1x H100-L, single-tenant VM for each run.
- Model: open-llm family medium (approx 12B), causal decoder. KV cache enabled.
- Workloads:
  - Knot bursts: N=600 sessions/sec for 30s windows, then idle 90s (duty 25%). Each session: 3 short turns (avg 30 tokens generate).
  - Steady: 200 qps sustained, 50-token average generate.
- Configs compared:
  A) tiling=on, slot_size=48ms, multiplex=false (tiling-only)
  B) tiling=on, multiplex=true, max_slots=64 (tiling+multiplex)
  C) tiling=off, multiplex=true, conservative batching (multiplex-only)
  D) baseline naively provisioned (no tiling, no multiplex, spawn-on-demand)
- Measurement: p50/p90/p99 latency (ms) for token stream start-to-first-token and end-to-end; tokens/sec observed; amortized cost estimate (USD per 1k generated tokens) using internal cost model.

Representative ASCII charts (aggregated across three 30-min runs each)
- Knot burst (30s window) latency summary (first-token p50/p90/p99):

  Config    | p50(ms) | p90(ms) | p99(ms) | tokens/s (burst) | est USD /1k tokens
  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  A (tiling)   |   68   |  140   |  420   |   11.3           |  0.86
  B (til+mx)   |   72   |  155   |  210   |   18.6           |  0.61
  C (mx only)  |  120   |  340   |  690   |    9.2           |  0.92
  D (baseline) |  320   |  860   | 1500   |    4.5           |  1.40

- Steady (sustained 200 qps) tokens/sec and p99 tail (end-to-end):

  Config    | stable tokens/s | p99 end-to-end (ms) | est USD /1k tokens
  ----------------------------------------------------------------
  A         |    9.5          |  320                | 0.94
  B         |   14.9          |  180                | 0.68
  C         |    8.8          |  520                | 0.98
  D         |    4.2          | 1400                | 1.53

Interpretation notes (quick takeaways)
- Tiling alone (A) reduces average latency vs baseline and improves cost modestly, but p99 spikes remain because tiling helps amortize compute only if slot alignment matches session arrivals.
- Multiplex combined with tiling (B) gives the best cost/throughput tradeoff for these short-turn workloads: higher tokens/s during burst windows and lower p99 compared to tiling-only. The multiplex scheduler reduces fragmentation and keeps GPU utilization higher during knots.
- Multiplex-only (C) can hurt tails in bursts: without tiling alignment, multiplex can create contention that increases p99 when many tiny sessions arrive simultaneously.
- Baseline (D) performs worst on tails and cost, as expected. Cold spawn and inefficient packing drive high p99 and low throughput.

Micro-observations (logs / runner notes)
- We saw 'slot drift' on tiling-only runs where several sessions repeatedly missed tile boundaries causing repeated pre-emption events. This accounted for ~18% of p99 samples in run A.
- In B, the combination of slightly larger slot_size and multiplex backpressure reduced pre-emption but introduced a small p50 inflation (approx 4ms). The p99 improvements outweighed that for our SLOs.
- Memory high-water marks: H100 run had consistently lower kv-cache flush count; A100 runs had intermittent KV eviction during worst knots.

Actionable suggestions for console UX / operator knobs (prioritized)
1) Add a 'knot-friendly' profile toggle in the console that sets: slot_size = 64ms, multiplex=true, multiplex_max_slots=64, prewarm_margin=0.15. Explain tradeoffs inline.
2) Surface recommended cost delta estimate per model/region: show est USD/1k tokens across 3 configs and a short bar showing p99 improvement.
3) Add a short-run synthetic knot benchmark in the capacity tab (30s bursts at tunable duty cycle) so teams can preview tail behavior.

Open questions and followups
- Need to test with larger models (30B) and multimodal workloads; early signals indicate tiling+mx still helps but cost curves shift.
- Evaluate effect of jittered arrival patterns (non-synchronous knots) — could reduce tiling boundary collisions.
- Confirm cost model across committed vs on-demand Dedicated pricing; our est USD/1k tokens assumes on-demand GPU pricing.

Quick A/B note for product copy (short)
- Suggested blurb for console: "Knot-friendly profile: up to 35% lower tail latency in short burst scenarios and 20-40% cost savings vs naive on-demand. Good for chat fronts and micro-conversational bursts."

Appendix: minimal run checklist
- Ensure KV cache enabled and pinned to model version.
- Warm model with 4 prewarm slots for 60s prior to knot run.
- Collect raw traces: trace ids CONS-3421-EX1..EX3.

Notes to self
- Save full traces to S3 bucket: s3://redwood-bench/burst-knots/sep15.
- Follow up with infra to run H100 multi-node replication next week.

End of draft.
